hypothesis: Author (2026-11-18): an organism may manage its resources for its species rather than for itself. AI translation in layer 3: the lifetime reserve per gram is set at species level by extrinsic mortality; flight lowers extrinsic mortality, so flying lineages spend more energy per gram over a lifetime. T018 found birds about 2.5 times above mammals (d_bird = 0.39 in log10). If flight, not class, sets the reserve, bats sit with the birds: d_bat > 0 and d_bat close to d_bird. Rate of living (no species-level allocation) gives d_bat = 0.

observable.quantity: bat offset d_bat and Delta = d_bat - d_bird in log10 LEP = a + s log10 M + d_bird [bird] + d_bat [Chiroptera]
observable.domain: AnAge Build 15 Aves and Mammalia selected exactly as in T018 (298 species: 128 birds, 24 bats, 146 other mammals)

prediction_method.description: Ordinary least squares of log10 LEP on log10 M, a bird indicator and a bat indicator; 95 percent percentile intervals from 10,000 species-level bootstrap resamples (seed 20261118), each resample required to contain at least one bat and one bird.

fixed_parameters: selection identical to T018; no species removed after the outcome is seen
metabolic rate as given by AnAge (resting or basal)
no phylogenetic correction (AI choice; makes intervals too narrow)
thresholds 0.18 (about 1.5 times) and 0.25 (about 1.8 times) fixed before the run
pass_criterion: PASS if the 95 percent interval of d_bat lies wholly above 0.18 and the 95 percent interval of Delta lies inside [-0.25, 0.25].
fail_criterion: FAILED if the upper end of the 95 percent interval of d_bat is below 0.18, or the 95 percent interval of Delta lies wholly outside [-0.25, 0.25]; INCONCLUSIVE otherwise.
note: Disclosure: not blind. Biology already reports that bats live long for their size (Austad and Fischer 1991, J. Gerontol. 46, B47; Brunet-Rossinni and Austad 2004; Wilkinson and South 2002) and that flight is linked to longevity in birds and bats (Matsuda and Makino 2024; Ikemoto et al. 2020). The 24 bats were inside the mammal group of T018, so they shaped that pooled fit, but no bat LEP was computed separately before drafting; only the counts (24 bats, 2 flightless birds) were read. Known bias in favour of PASS: many bats hibernate or use daily torpor, so a resting metabolic rate times maximum longevity overstates their lifetime energy; AnAge has no hibernation field to correct this, so a PASS cannot separate species-level allocation from torpor. Nearest theory: disposable soma (Kirkwood 1977) and extrinsic-mortality theory of ageing; a PASS would show layer 3 can carry a species-level reserve, not a UET-distinct result. The two flightless birds are reported only.
